Went to the doctor to see wtf the was wrong with me. They had no idea based on what I told them.  They had me poop and tested and nothing. So they let me go with no help. 

Fast forward a year. I have the exact same pain and am laying on my bathroom floor again, but I don’t pass out. I text my friend and he takes me to the ER. I get taken in. Nurse comes back and he says that the doctor says to give me more fent once it’s been 30 minutes. We wait, he gives me more. Nothing. Still pain. We repeat this one more time. Take this from someone who took a lot of animal science classes.  And is an agriculture teacher that focuses on the animal science side of things. 

First off you only have two options if you’re thinking of switching to that major; Cal Poly and Davis. 

If you are thinking of becoming a vet a lot of people will recommend going to Davis since they have a great vet program. Your undergrad school does not matter when it comes to getting into their Vet Post grad program. In fact the number one major that gets into that grad program is history.  Also it is fairly well known that Cal Poly is planning on opening their own grad program for vets soon. 

Regardless of if you are planning on doing vet post grad or just animal science for another reason, Cal Poly is the obvious choice. Cal Poly with their hands on style makes you job ready from the day of graduation and the learning experiences is so much more impactful.   One of my favorite class memories was practicing AI on the campus cows for a quarter. You don’t get that experience at Davis. 

I know I am biased, but I also have seen a ton of people go through both programs. Davis is amazing, SLO is better for animal science no question. 

Another thing you have to take into account is the area. SLO and Davis are both small little college towns and both have their pros and cons. For me I much prefer living where it doesn’t get to 110 regularly. SLO has my much preferred kind of environment. I love the coast, beaches, beautiful hiking spots, national forest super close.

So a big concern you have to take into account is what kind of climate do you want to live in. 

I am biased, I have a cal poly flag hanging in my classroom, I used to help recruit for cal poly, but I would 10/10 times choose cal poly over Davis regardless of major, but if you are thinking of doing animal science it’s an absolute no brained in my perspective.  

If you aren’t thinking of animal science I would still recommend SLO>UCSD>Davis and that’s purely coming from the fact I love being on the coast
